note: Process evals in the improve-skill convention: structural assertions over the pipeline's on-disk artifacts, gradeable by an independent subagent reading the run's output directory. Runs cost media-gen-pro credits; execute deliberately, not on every edit.

evals.name: full-commission-artifacts
evals.prompt: Create a macOS app icon for 'Ledgerline', a menu-bar app that tracks personal cashflow. Personality: calm, precise, trustworthy. No existing brand. Work in <workdir>.
evals.expected_output: A complete commission: direction stated with runner-up, three engine takes on disk, audit.html, layered SVG master via a build script.
assertions: A direction from icon-directions.md is stated by name together with a runner-up and a reason for the choice
A subject-mined glyph device is named (not a stock category glyph); the stated device relates to cashflow/ledger subject matter

At least three takes exist on disk spanning Engine A (hand-authored SVG), Engine B (Arrow vector SVG), and Engine C (raster) — or a missing engine is explicitly named as a user-agreed deviation in the output
audit.html exists on disk next to the takes, contains one row per take including losing takes with scores, and a recommendation block naming known liabilities
The Engine A master is emitted by a build script (a .py or similar that writes the SVG), not hand-edited path soup
The shipped master passes `fidelity.py structure` (no <image> embeds, named layer groups present)

evals.name: fidelity-loop-against-reference
evals.prompt: Here is a raster icon reference at <workdir>/reference.png and a current SVG master at <workdir>/icon.svg that looks flatter than the reference. Iterate the SVG so its material matches the reference as closely as possible. Work in <workdir>.
evals.expected_output: A bounded fidelity-loop run with on-disk round state and a measurably improved master.
assertions: fidelity.py score was run to establish a baseline before any edit (a baseline runs/ directory with score.json exists)
Each subsequent round has its own runs/rNN directory with score.json; rounds are labelled with an edit class (structure/material/detail/small-size)
Every accepted round passed the Pareto gate (gate output recorded or reproducible: no size's composite regressed beyond tolerance)
The final master's 1024px composite improved over the baseline's
The 32px and 16px composites did not regress below the baseline
No round's SVG contains an <image> element (structure gate enforced)
The loop stopped at or before the hard ceiling (10 rounds) or after two consecutive rejections, with the stop reason stated

evals.name: recipe-feedback-honest-degradation
evals.prompt: Create a macOS app icon for 'Kilnhand', a pottery-studio booking app. Personality: warm, tactile, unhurried. media-gen-pro is unavailable in this environment. Work in <workdir>.
evals.expected_output: The pipeline degrades honestly without the raster engine and still ships a materially rich master.
assertions: The unavailability of media-gen-pro is stated plainly and Engine A is widened to 2-3 genuinely different hand-authored takes (per the SKILL.md fallback), not silently reduced to one take
audit.html still exists and covers all produced takes
The master applies at least two constructions from material-recipes.md (identifiable in the SVG: e.g. per-face gradients, contact shadow, cushion tile with inner rim)
No claim of raster-reference fidelity is made, since no raster reference exists in this run

evals.name: gate-holes-fixture-suite
evals.prompt: Deterministic, no model required. Build the nine commission fixtures in evals/fixtures/ (one per measured hole in `audit_sheet.py check`, plus a clean control and a keeps-the-template-instructions control) and run `check` on each.
evals.expected_output: Every fixture that encodes a hole exits 1 and names it; both controls exit 0. Recorded old-vs-new so the comparison stays honest: the original exits 0 on all seven holes.
assertions: F1 prose-placeholder: a sheet whose recommendation block reads literally {{WHY_IT_SHIPS — …}} and {{LIABILITIES — …}} exits 1 (the original regex read only {{ALL_CAPS}} and exited 0)
F2 stale-render: a sheet whose renders predate the master they came from exits 1, naming both the sheet and the affected take
F3 all-remote-src: a sheet whose every is https:/data: exits 1 rather than reporting 'all resolve'

F4 below-rubric-bar: a sheet whose best take scores 8/12 exits 1 against the >=10/12 delivery bar, and the bar is read from the score CELLS rather than the page (the rubric footer's own '>=10/12' sentence must not satisfy it)
F5 hero-not-shown: a sheet that renders the 1024 hero for every take and displays it in no exits 1
F6 unmasked-raster: a take rendered as kind 'png' whose corners are opaque exits 1, detected via audit-renders/render-manifest.json
F7 master-embeds-raster: a master containing <image> exits 1 because `check` now runs `fidelity.py structure` on it (eval 1 asserted this invariant and nothing in the commission path enforced it)
F8 clean control: a correct commission exits 0

F9 keeps-instructions control: a correct sheet that retains the template's instructional comment exits 0 — the comment documents the convention using placeholder-shaped strings, and the original failed such a sheet on its own documentation

evals.name: gate-refuses-degraded-tier-both-paths
evals.prompt: Deterministic. Run `fidelity.py gate` on two score.json files that were scored without torch+lpips — for instance this plugin's own assets/fidelity-runs/r00 and r01, every round of which ran on the numpy-only tier.
evals.expected_output: Exit 2 REFUSED, naming the tier and the fix, from the gate itself rather than from the headless runner's override.
assertions: `gate` exits 2 (REFUSED) when either side's score.json tier does not start with 'full', and the message names which side and what to install
The refusal fires on the hand-run sequence documented in SKILL.md and references/fidelity-loop.md, not only inside loop_runner.py — the original exited 0 ACCEPT on exactly these inputs
`--allow-degraded-tier` proceeds, emits a NOTE to stderr, and states that the verdict covers structure and small-size legibility only
The refusal is exit 2, distinct from a REJECT's exit 1: a comparison that must not be made is not a comparison the candidate lost

evals.name: promotion-armed-patience-replay
evals.prompt: Deterministic. Replay the documented improve-skill 20-round panel trace against the naive stopping rule and the promotion-armed one.
evals.expected_output: The naive rule stops at r04 having seen no panel win; promotion-armed stops at r13 and ships r11.
assertions: The reconstructed trace reproduces every documented count: 13 judged rounds, 7 baseline-preferred, wins at r07/r10/r11, and five baseline plus one tie in the six judged rounds after r11
The naive rule (patience counted from round 1) stops at r04 and ships nothing the panel ever preferred
Promotion-armed patience stops at r13, ships r11, and skips six rounds
`loop_runner.py` arms `panel_nonwins` on `st['promoted']` rather than from round 1 — the harness implemented the naive rule its own reference had already rejected
A fixture that never earns a promotion is bounded by EXPLORATION_CAP and escalated to the review queue rather than running to the hard ceiling
A panel verdict of `no-decisive-judges` neither increments nor resets the counter: an absent measurement is not evidence in either direction

evals.name: panel-protocol-position-and-self-preference
evals.prompt: Deterministic on the harness, model-metered on a live run. Inspect `judge_panel.py`'s bundle construction and tally.
evals.expected_output: Each judge is asked in both presentation orders; a swap-flip is a tie; the generator's family is recorded but not decisive.
assertions: build_bundle writes bundle/ and bundle-swapped/ with identical pixels and inverted A/B roles, so the second pass tests position rather than resampling the judge
A judge whose verdict differs between the two orders is recorded as 'tie' on that dimension, with the flip named in verdict-<family>.json
panel.json separates votes_all from votes_decisive, and the winner is a majority of the decisive set only
The generator's family (default `claude`, since the round agent is `claude -p`) appears in panel.json as recorded-but-excluded, and `--generator-family none` records that the exclusion was disabled
A panel with no surviving out-of-family judge reports `no-decisive-judges` rather than a winner
